> There doesn't seem to be clear documentation on the expected behavior, so this may not be a bug. It does, however, differ in behavior compared to other languages like javascript.

This is described in the [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html#lambda-functions). Local variables are captured by value. This means that modifying captured variables in a lambda only works for reference types (for example, if you change the contents of an array). Reassigning a captured variable within the lambda body does not change the outer local variable. This is due to the lifetime of local variables (GDScript does not have a garbage collector). See https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8558 for details.

In the second code fragment, the line `x += 1` generates the `CONFUSABLE_CAPTURE_REASSIGNMENT` warning. Regarding the first code snippet, I'm not sure I fully understood what you meant, but I think you meant the opposite case: captured local variables aren't updated in the lambda after it's created when you modify their originals outside. In this case, I don't think we can add any warning; that's just how capture-by-value works.

> This is described in the [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html#lambda-functions).

D'oh! I completely missed that. This is why you never skip reading the warnings 🤦.

> Regarding the first code snippet, I'm not sure I fully understood what you meant, but I think you meant the opposite case: captured local variables aren't updated in the lambda after it's created when you modify their originals outside.

That's exactly what I meant. Apologies for the confusion and lack of use for proper terminology.

Regardless, it seems like this "issue" is accounted for. Thanks for the input.

Can you suggest how we could improve the existing documentation or language behavior without breaking compatibility (via warnings, etc.)? If not, let's close this issue, as it's not actionable and there's the proposal https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8558 already tracking this language design flaw.

I was primarily referencing the [Callable documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_callable.html) rather than the [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html#lambda-functions) you provided (my fault for skimming the basics).

I'm not sure if it'd be appropriate to include the warning in the Callable documentation, since this issue seems specific to lambdas. It may be worth mentioning a similar warning in Callable or linking back to lambda documentation warning.
